questions.rationale: Both candidates state the two inertial-frame postulates, all physical laws rather than mechanics only, no privileged inertial frame, and invariant vacuum c independent of source or observer motion. This matches the frozen independent derivation. Available n95 corroborates physical-law equivalence and invariant vacuum c; the requested n94 contract remains unavailable.

Both candidates explicitly distinguish mechanics-only inertial equivalence from equivalence for all physical laws, including electromagnetism. No false reference-frame privilege is introduced. Content matches the independent scope derivation, but the specified canonical n94 cannot be read or hashed.

The candidates use local synchronized clocks in a chosen frame and distinguish event time from uncorrected signal reception. The qualification 'generally' avoids falsely saying all spatially separated simultaneous events become nonsimultaneous under every boost. This agrees with n95 p0254#3 and its frame-dependent simultaneity discussion.

Both define proper time for the same event pair at one spatial location, recorded by a single rest clock, then give tau=gamma*tau_0 for a uniformly moving inertial frame using synchronized clocks and |v|<c. They do not confuse clock-local proper time with reception times or make an unrestricted accelerated-path minimum claim. The definition is complete without requiring an extra numerical example.

The full question spanning p0263#11 and p0264#1 is retained as one identity. Both answers distinguish a local proper-time clock from spatially separated synchronized coordinate clocks, explicitly select a different event pair when exchanging clocks, invoke relativity of simultaneity, and retain frame equivalence. They do not apply inverse inequalities to one unchanged event pair or explain the effect solely by signal delay.

Both identify the source's short-lived-particle decay experiment with charged pi mesons, contrast rest or slowly moving mean lifetimes with high-speed laboratory mean lifetimes, and state tau=gamma*tau_0 with statistical rather than identical per-particle lifetimes. They do not substitute muons, invent a named first-discovery experiment, or make false fixed lifetime/distance/light-speed claims. The question asks which experiment, so omitted optional numerical examples are not incompleteness.

Both specify a rigid rod aligned with its uniform motion, fixed proper length, subluminal relative speed, same-time endpoint measurements using the measuring frame's synchronized clocks, and the correct l=l_0*sqrt(1-v^2/c^2). Both describe shortening with speed magnitude, the v=0 limit, and no transverse contraction. These conditions agree with both specified repaired n97 definitions.

Both require the frame speed and object speed in the moving frame to be much smaller than vacuum c, identify |v_1*v|/c^2 as negligible, preserve the current lesson's velocity roles, and explicitly give an approximate classical sum rather than an arbitrary-speed exact identity. This agrees with the original n98 formula and p0263#1.
